native_result.query: In which century do Diversity in Pottery Decoration and Diversity in Pottery Form show opposite growth trends for the first time, with Pottery Decoration increasing significantly and Pottery Form declining simultaneously?
native_result.HypoA: In 1700 BCE, for the first time, Diversity in Pottery Decoration shows a significant increase while Diversity in Pottery Form experiences a notable decline. This marks a unique divergence in the growth trends of these two cultural capital variables.
native_result.HypoB: The first century in which Diversity in Pottery Decoration and Diversity in Pottery Form show opposite growth trends — with Pottery Decoration rising significantly and Pottery Form declining simultaneously — is the 17th century BCE (the bin labelled "BCE 1700" in capital.csv, covering 1700–1601 BCE under the upper-edge bin convention). Over the boundary from the BCE 1800 bin (Late Neolithic) into the BCE 1700 bin (Older Bronze Age), Pottery Decoration diversity increases by ΔZ = +1.45 σ (Zkeverz going from −0.48 to +0.97) while Pottery Form diversity decreases by ΔZ = −1.87 σ (ZKeform going from +0.74 to −1.13). This is the only opposite-sign transition in the entire 4300–500 BCE range and is unambiguously the first such century; the candidate remains unique at every significance threshold tested (|Δ| > τ for τ ∈ {0.05, 0.10, 0.25, 0.50} σ) and is robust to ±1-year bin-alignment perturbation.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Plan-stage inspection (artifacts/plan_inspection.py): confirmed schema (PotteryForm/PotteryForm_inter/PotteryDecoration/PotteryDecoration_inter in time_series_data.csv; BCE/ZKeform/Zkeverz in capital.csv), row counts (3601 annual; 39 centennial), ranges (CE -4100..-500; BCE 4300..500), and that time_series raw values reproduce capital.csv exactly at all 37 aligned years. 2) Main analysis (artifacts/main_analysis.py): primary scan on capital.csv oldest->youngest over 38 consecutive 100y bins computes Δ = newer_bin - older_bin for both series and flags transitions with ΔDecoration>0 and ΔForm<0 at |Δ|>0.10σ (sensitivity 0.05/0.25/0.50). Exactly one boundary qualifies, BCE 1800 -> BCE 1700 (ΔDec=+1.450σ, ΔForm=-1.870σ). 3) Cross-check: sampling time_series_data.csv Pottery*_inter at the upper-edge year (CE=-BCE) of each capital.csv row reproduces 37/37 mappable rows within 1e-6 (the two oldest capital rows BCE 4300/4200 pre-date the CE=-4100 floor of time_series_data.csv). ±1-year cross-check offsets also yield the same first century (BCE 1700).
